value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes the City of Orange/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Express Checklist for Residential Solar Photovoltaic and Energy Storage System (uploaded to the Civic Portal and present at all inspections)

required_documents.notes: The Express Checklist form itself (a PDF) triggers a file-download dialog rather than a viewable page and could not be read for its itemized content; its existence and required use are confirmed via the City's own 'Building Inspections' page, which lists it among items that 'shall be present at the time of inspections.'

value: Contractor must be onsite at the time of inspection
A copy of the submitted plans, the uploaded Express Checklist, and the electrical single line diagram must be present at every inspection
If the installation or onsite conditions differ from what was submitted and permitted, revise drawings and upload them to the portal prior to the next scheduled inspection
If batteries are installed within a structure, Fire Department inspection and approval is required (714-288-2546 or 714-288-2536)
A ladder is required for inspection of the solar arrays and roof access clearances
No job card is needed onsite; all approvals are available in the Civic Portal
